title: Further question: one act adorning image and exemplar together? Peresius and Catharinus deny
source_text: XLIX. Praeterea quaeritur inter Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae An uno & eodem adorationis actu imago & exemplar simul adorari possint & debeant, nempe dum consideratur exemplar tanquam imagine vestitum, imago vero ut exemplar continens, & ipso velut animata; ita ut in adorantis mente imago & exemplar unum quid constituant. Hunc Imagines adorandi modum quidam ex Doctoribus Scholae Romanae non agnoscunt, & imaginis adorationem existimant semper actum esse diversum ab eo quo ipsum exemplar adoratur. Quae est opinio Martini Peresii de Ayala libro de Traditionibus ubi de cultu imaginum agit, & Ambrosii Catharini opusculo singulari de adoratione imaginum, ut testantur Vasquez & Suarez disputationibus saepius jam citatis.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, it is asked among the Doctors of the Roman Church Whether by one and the same act of adoration the image and the exemplar can and ought to be adored together, namely when the exemplar is considered as clothed with the image, and the image as containing the exemplar and as it were animated by it; so that in the mind of the adorant the image and the exemplar constitute one something. This mode of adoring Images certain of the Doctors of the Roman School do not acknowledge, and they judge the adoration of the image always to be an act diverse from that by which the exemplar itself is adored. Which is the opinion of Martinus Peresius de Ayala in the book On Traditions where he treats of the cult of images, and of Ambrosius Catharinus in a singular little work on the adoration of images, as Vasquez and Suarez testify in the disputationes so often already cited.
pass_b_english: Next quarrel: can one act adore image and exemplar together as one mental object?
Peresius de Ayala and Ambrosius Catharinus say no—image-adoration is always a distinct act from exemplar-adoration.

lemmas.gloss: by one and the same act of adoration
